prompt:
Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

Every category has a bidirectional nature. For example:

One person's sensitivity to the Care/Harm foundation may lead them to support high levels of immigration from poorer nations, to reduce the suffering of those who migrate. Whereas another person's sensitivity to the very same foundation may lead them to oppose those levels, because they believe it could lead to people they care about being harmed.

TEXT_E:
Forward, Together sets out a mainstream Conservative plan to steer Britain through its most challenging five years in decades. With strong and stable leadership, the UK will secure a smooth, orderly Brexit, strengthen the Union, and build a Great Meritocracy where hard work and talent determine success.

Core principles and challenges
- Govern for ordinary, working families; reject extremes of the socialist left and libertarian right; use government as a force for good.
- Tackle five giant challenges: securing a strong economy; delivering Brexit in a changing world; overcoming social divisions; responding to an ageing society; harnessing fast-changing technology.

A strong economy that works for everyone
- Sound finances and low taxes; personal allowance to £12,500 and higher rate to £50,000 by 2020; no VAT rise; corporation tax to 17%.
- Modern Industrial Strategy: lift R&D to 2.4% of GDP within 10 years; £23bn National Productivity Investment Fund; “Future Britain” sovereign-style funds.
- Back SMEs; reform business rates; strengthen worker rights including in the gig economy; raise the National Living Wage.
- Fairer corporate governance: shareholder votes on pay, publish pay ratios, worker voice on boards; tougher rules on takeovers and pensions abuse; crack down on tax evasion.
- Competitive energy with an independent Cost of Energy review; protect consumers with a safeguard tariff cap; diverse mix including offshore wind and responsible shale development.
- Major infrastructure: HS2, Northern Powerhouse Rail, Heathrow expansion; EV ambition (nearly all cars/vans zero-emission by 2050).

A strong, united nation and Global Britain
- Preserve the Union; increase devolved powers post‑Brexit; move civil service and cultural bodies beyond London; UK Shared Prosperity Fund to level up communities.
- Brexit: leave the single market and customs union; seek a deep and special partnership with the EU; Great Repeal Bill to bring EU law into UK law; control immigration; uphold workers’ rights.
- Global leadership: champion free trade; maintain 0.7% aid with better rules; lead on climate, modern slavery and data ethics.
- Defence and security: meet NATO 2% and rise in real terms; retain Trident; invest £178bn in equipment; stronger policing, counter-terror and cyber.

The world’s Great Meritocracy
- More good school places: 100+ free schools a year; lift ban on new selective schools with safeguards; universities and independent schools to support state schools; knowledge-rich curriculum.
- World-class technical education: new T-levels, institutes of technology; 3 million apprenticeships; lifelong digital and career learning.
- Controlled, sustainable migration: net migration down to the tens of thousands; high standards for students; align visas with industrial strategy.
- Confront burning injustices: narrow gender and race pay gaps; new Mental Health Bill and workplace duties; 1m more disabled people in work; landmark Domestic Violence and Abuse Bill; halve rough sleeping.

A restored contract between generations
- Fiscal credibility; new “Double Lock” on state pensions from 2020; fair, sustainable social care: include housing in means test with a £100k asset floor and no forced home sale in lifetime; means‑test Winter Fuel Payments.
- NHS: at least £8bn extra over five years; more staff and training; modern buildings and technology; seven‑day services; 10,000 more mental health professionals.
- Homes for all: 1.5m homes by 2022; protect Green Belt; council housing deals; fixed‑term social homes with a new Right to Buy.

Prosperity and security in a digital age
- Digital Charter: best place to start and grow a digital business; safest place online.
- Universal broadband, full-fibre expansion, 5G rollout; stronger data rights, a Data Use and Ethics Commission, modern data protection law; drop Leveson 2 and repeal Section 40.
- Digital government by default, open data, and smarter infrastructure.

This is a confident, long‑term Conservative plan to go forward, together.

TEXT_F:
Labour Party Manifesto 2017 – For the many, not the few (summary)

Labour sets out a choice to end a “rigged” status quo by rebuilding a fair economy and strong public services through investment, public accountability and rights at work.

Economy, tax and investment
- Upgrade the economy with a £250bn National Transformation Fund over 10 years and a National Investment Bank leveraging £250bn of lending, focused on all regions and small businesses.
- Fiscal Credibility Rule: eliminate the day‑to‑day deficit within five years while borrowing to invest; debt lower by the end of the Parliament.
- Fair tax: no rises in income tax for 95% (those under £80k), no rises in VAT or personal NICs; top 5% and large corporations pay a bit more; clamp down on avoidance; protect and simplify for small firms.

Industrial strategy and ownership
- Mission-led strategy: 60% of energy from zero/renewable by 2030; 3% of GDP on R&D by 2030; skills, infrastructure and procurement reshaped to drive high-wage, high-skill jobs.
- Widen democratic ownership: double the co‑operative sector; “right to own” for employees; insource public services.
- Bring rail, water and Royal Mail into public ownership as contracts allow; regain control of energy networks and build a decentralised, publicly owned energy system.

Energy and climate
- Immediate household energy price cap while reforming the market.
- Insulate 4m homes; interest‑free loans for homeowners; stronger standards for renters.
- Ban fracking; back renewables and tidal lagoons; support nuclear within climate goals.
- New Clean Air Act; protect habitats; ban neonicotinoids; plant 1m native trees.

Brexit, trade and immigration
- Jobs‑first Brexit prioritising Single Market and Customs Union benefits; reject “no deal”; meaningful vote in Parliament.
- Guarantee EU nationals’ rights and reciprocal UK rights; no hard Irish border.
- Pro‑trade with high standards, transparency and SME support; human rights at the core.
- Fair migration rules ending scapegoating; crack down on exploitation; restore Migrant Impact Fund; welcome international students.

Education and skills
- National Education Service: cradle‑to‑grave, free at point of use in FE; abolish university tuition fees and restore maintenance grants.
- Expand funded early years, extend 30 free hours to two‑year‑olds, strengthen Sure Start.
- Reverse school cuts; cap infant class sizes at under 30; free primary meals; end teacher pay cap; reduce high‑stakes testing.

Work, rights and incomes
- 20‑point plan: ban zero‑hours contracts; day‑one rights; sectoral bargaining; abolish tribunal fees; Living Wage £10 by 2020; end public sector pay cap; 20:1 pay ratio on public contracts; strengthen equality and union rights; tackle bogus self‑employment.

Social security and pensions
- Keep the triple lock; protect universal pensioner benefits; fair transitional support for WASPI women.
- Scrap sanctions, Bedroom Tax, and punitive cuts; redesign Universal Credit; strengthen disability support under the UNCRPD; humane, holistic assessments.

Homes
- Build over 1m homes; at least 100k council/HA homes a year by end of Parliament.
- Private renters: three‑year tenancies, inflation‑linked rent caps, ban letting fees, minimum standards.
- Suspend Right to Buy where homes aren’t replaced; end rough sleeping with 4,000 homes and prevention.

NHS and care
- Over £30bn extra for the NHS; end pay cap; restore bursaries; reverse privatisation; guarantee 18‑week treatment and 4‑hour A&E targets; free hospital parking.
- Ring‑fence mental health; end out‑of‑area placements; school counselling.
- Build a National Care Service: £8bn this Parliament plus a long‑term funding settlement; real Living Wage for carers; end 15‑minute visits; cap lifetime care costs.

Safer, cleaner, connected communities
- 10,000 more police; 3,000 firefighters; 500 border guards; tackle violence against women and girls; rebuild youth services and local assets.
- Transport: bring rail into public ownership; cap fares; expand bus franchising/municipal buses; complete HS2, Northern Powerhouse Rail/Crossrail 2; nationwide electrification; boost cycling/walking; clean vehicles.

Democracy and equality
- Constitutional Convention; votes at 16; reform Lords; extend FOI; repeal Lobbying Act.
- Strengthen EHRC; gender audit of policy; 50% women cabinet; advance LGBT, BAME and disability rights (including UNCRPD into law).

Global Britain
- Foreign policy rooted in peace, human rights and international law; recognise Palestine; suspend arms sales for use in Yemen pending UN investigation; climate leadership.
- Defence: spend at least 2% of GDP; renew Trident; strategic review; support UN peacekeeping; invest in UK defence industry and Armed Forces’ pay and housing.
- Development: keep 0.7% aid; tackle tax havens; support universal health coverage.

A programme to rebuild a fairer Britain that works for the many, not the few.
